I pulled traces and sampling from the evening window. Preliminary findings:
- We see a sharp increase in decoder kernel fallbacks to the slower FP32 path when sequences exceed ~3.5k tokens for certain conversations. That triggers higher per-token execution time and increases queueing at the tokenization layer.
- A subset of requests (approx 6–8% of the sampled traffic) experienced KV cache misses due to unusually long prefixes, causing full re-compute on the model side.
- Edge 502s line up with short-lived overload on the request broker; concurrent per-worker queue depth spiked beyond our batch/queue SLOs.

Immediate mitigations (can be applied now, ~10–25m):
1) Flip model routing to the lighter quantized variant for Acme's API key (quick config change) — drops p99 by ~30–40% in tests.
2) Reduce batch aggregation window from 20ms -> 10ms for the affected workers to lower tail under burst (small throughput hit).
3) Enable conservative per-key concurrency throttle (limit 8 concurrent streams per key) to avoid broker saturation — prefer temporary, customer-specific throttle.

I am opening PD incident POD-8293 and will push changes in the next 12 minutes. We should monitor for improved p99 in the evening window. If that doesn't recover, recommend failover to Dedicated pool (if customer consents).

Karthik
